# Results — Study 845 (Stadium Naming-Rights Curse)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**managerial hubris / peak-earnings signaling**: a company that buys expensive stadium
naming rights is spending shareholder cash on a vanity trophy near a self-confident
peak, and subsequently **underperforms** (folklore's poster children: Enron, WorldCom,
FTX). Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce
every number. Stamped **as-of 2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the
partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `d8056fdb1c84` (SPY); per-sponsor
fingerprints printed by `verify.py`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily total-return closes: SPY (7,419 rows, 1997-01-02 → 2026-06-30) + **28** listed sponsor tickers (each from its own listing start; ADRs where the parent is foreign) |
| Deal table | **hardcoded** table of **34** major US/European stadium & arena naming-rights deals, 1997-12 → 2023-06, cross-referenced against each venue's public naming-rights record (see references.md) |
| Tradable split | **29** deals have a listed sponsor; **5** are untradable cautionary tales — **Enron Field** (bankrupt 2001), **MCI Center / WorldCom** (fraud, bankrupt 2002), **FTX Arena** & **Crypto.com Arena** (private crypto exchanges), **SoFi Stadium** (private at the deal). These are the folklore's poster children and have **no usable price tape** — kept in the table, named honestly, excluded from the return test |
| Coverage | of the 29 tradable, **28** load (Comerica / **CMA** has no Yahoo tape — a named no-coverage drop, never zero-filled) |
| Statistic | **buy-and-hold abnormal return** (BHAR, Barber & Lyon 1997): (sponsor total return) − (SPY total return) over the 252-session (1-yr) and 504-session (2-yr) window after the deal. One-sample *t* across deals (primary), a Newey-West *t* (calendar-clustering cross-check), a Wilson hit-rate interval, a sub-era split, a random-entry-date placebo, and a costed short-the-sponsor overlay |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: the announcement date is snapped to the first NYSE session on/after it (zero look-ahead — the deal is public by that close). The overlay shorts the sponsor & longs SPY: 2 legs × one-way cost × NAV on entry+exit (4 × `cost_bps`) + borrow on the short pro-rated to the window |
| Survivorship (named on the Signal axis) | the tradable sample **excludes the sponsors that actually went to zero** (Enron, WorldCom) — no free full-path tape exists for them. The measured "curse" is therefore an **understatement** of the folklore's worst cases: even the *survivors* underperform |

## The headline — 1-year sponsor BHAR vs SPY

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| mean sponsor BHAR (n=28) | **−11.26%** |
| median | −18.02% |
| one-sample *t* | **−2.54** |
| Newey-West *t* (lags=4) | **−2.41** |
| hit rate (sponsor < SPY) | **21/28 = 75.0%** (Wilson 95% [56.6%, 87.3%]) |
| random-entry placebo | observed −11.26% vs placebo mean **+5.75%** (sd 10.91%), **left-tail p = 0.003** over 3,000 draws |

On the first year after buying a stadium's name, the average listed sponsor
**underperforms the S&P 500 by 11.3 percentage points** — a *t* of −2.54 that survives
a calendar-clustering-robust Newey-West standard error (−2.41), a 3-out-of-4 hit rate,
and a random-entry placebo (a random date on the *same names* beats this outcome only
0.3% of the time; note the placebo's mean is **+5.75%** — these large-cap survivors
normally *beat* SPY at a random entry, which makes the −11.3% post-deal reading all the
more against type). Taken alone, this clears the desk's |*t*| ≥ 2 bar.

## Why it is **not** stamped Real — the robustness the claim fails

| robustness cut | result |
|---|--:|
| **2-year window** | mean **−10.91%**, *t* = **−1.82** (NW −1.69), hit 60.7%, placebo p = 0.022 — **below the bar** |
| **sub-era: pre-2010** (n=12) | mean −5.96%, *t* = **−0.84** — no effect |
| **sub-era: post-2010** (n=16) | mean −15.24%, *t* = −2.70 — the whole effect lives here |
| **drop the single worst name** | *t* = −2.26 (still ≥ 2) |
| **drop the two worst** (Caesars −50%, Allegiant −39%) | *t* = **−1.99** — falls under the bar |
| **drop the four worst** | *t* = −1.46 |
| **leave-one-out jackknife** | *t* ∈ [−3.12, −2.26] (no single deletion flips it, but the tail is thin) |

The desk's Real bar requires an era-robust |*t*| ≥ 2 on the real tape. This signal
**fails three ways**: it evaporates at the 2-year horizon (*t* = −1.82), it is entirely
a **post-2010** phenomenon (pre-2010 *t* = −0.84), and it is **tail-driven** — removing
just the two worst names (Caesars and Allegiant, both stadium sponsors that were then
gutted by the 2020 COVID shock) drops it below significance. Six of the sixteen
post-2010 deals cluster in **2019–2021**, immediately before a pandemic and a
rate-shock that mauled airlines, casinos and regional banks — hubris, or a run of
sponsors that happened to sign right before a sector crisis? At n=28 the two are not
separable.

## The individual sponsors — the "curse" is a fat left tail, not a uniform drag

| worst 1-yr BHAR | | best 1-yr BHAR | |
|---|--:|---|--:|
| Caesars (Superdome, 2021) | −49.99% | Toyota (Toyota Center, 2003) | +37.96% |
| Allegiant (Allegiant Stadium, 2019) | −39.37% | FedEx (FedExField, 1998) | +35.58% |
| Truist (Truist Park, 2019) | −35.29% | JPMorgan (Chase Center, 2016) | +31.87% |
| Citigroup (Citi Field, 2006) | −34.23% | | |
| Ball Corp (Ball Arena, 2020) | −31.42% | | |
| Barclays (Barclays Center, 2007) | −31.16% | | |

The distribution is **left-skewed**: a cluster of sponsors (Caesars, Allegiant, Truist,
Citi, Ball, Barclays) cratered 30–50% in the year after their deal, while the best
outcomes (Toyota, FedEx, JPMorgan) only gained ~30–38%. Several of the worst are
financials and cyclicals that signed just before a crisis (Citi and Barclays → the 2008
GFC; Caesars, Allegiant, Truist, Ball → the 2020 COVID / 2022 rate shock). That is the
honest ambiguity: the folklore's mechanism (hubris) and a mundane one (crisis-timing
bad luck, concentrated in cyclical sponsors) predict the same left tail here.

## The tradable overlay — "short the cursed sponsor, long SPY"

Enter at the announcement's first tradable close, short the sponsor and long SPY for the
window; 2 legs × one-way cost × NAV on entry+exit plus borrow on the short.

| window | gross | net (5 bps + 100 bps/yr borrow) | *t* (net) | win rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-year | +11.26% | **+10.06%** | **+2.27** | 71% |
| 2-year | +10.91% | +8.71% | +1.45 | 61% |

The 1-year overlay nets a positive **+10.1%** per deal (*t* = 2.27) — but this is
**Fragile**, not investable: it is the same non-robust 1-year signal in a costume, it
dies at 2 years (*t* = 1.45), and it requires *shorting exactly the names that are
hardest and most expensive to borrow* — Caesars and the crypto-adjacent, high-short-
interest sponsors that drive the tail. Real borrow on those names in a crisis dwarfs the
100 bps/yr charged here. Roughly one deal per year over 25 years is also far too few
independent bets to underwrite a short book.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic sponsor + SPY random-walk tapes with a TUNABLE planted post-deal
underperformance (`edge`), martingale-corrected so the null BHAR is mean-zero; no
network.

| world | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.26** (sd 1.08), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** (~the 5% expected rate) |
| planted curse edge = −25% (seed 845) | mean −17.7%, **t = −3.66** |

The detector sits at zero on the null and lights up sharply, with the correct negative
sign, on a planted curse. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in
support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The 1-year post-deal BHAR is **−11.3%** (*t* = −2.54, NW −2.41,
  75% hit, placebo **p = 0.003**) — a real, correctly-signed, placebo-significant
  underperformance that is **more than the Enron/FTX cherry-pick** (even the surviving,
  tradable sponsors lag). But it is **not Real**: it vanishes by the 2-year horizon
  (*t* = −1.82), it is entirely a post-2010 effect (pre-2010 *t* = −0.84), and it falls
  below the bar when the two COVID-hit tail names are removed (*t* = −1.99). With n=28,
  a survivorship-trimmed sample (the actual bankruptcies are excluded), and a 2019–2021
  crisis cluster, hubris and bad-timing luck are not separable. Suggestive, not certified.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** A short-the-sponsor overlay nets +10.1% at 1 year
  (*t* = 2.27) but dies at 2 years, rides the same non-robust tail, and would require
  shorting the least-borrowable names in exactly the crises that produce the payoff.
  Not bankable.
- **"Does buying a stadium's name curse the sponsor?" — MIXED.** Not pure folklore —
  the systematic 1-year underperformance is real and survives a placebo — but not the
  robust law the anecdotes imply: it is one era, a fat left tail of crisis-timed
  cyclicals, and a handful of names, on top of a sample that already excludes the very
  blow-ups (Enron, WorldCom) that started the legend.
